cloudflare_meeting: A RealtimeKit meeting -- a scheduled or ad-hoc video/audio session. Configures recording (`record_on_start`, `recording_config`), transcription and AI-generated summaries (`ai_config`, `transcribe_on_end`, `summarize_on_end`), and live-streaming behavior for the session.
cloudflare_memory: An Agent Memory namespace -- an isolated storage space for an AI agent's own persistent memory records, identified by `namespace_name` (optionally scoped to a `profile_name`). The same real endpoint and shape as cloudflare_namespace, discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec.
cloudflare_namespace: An Agent Memory namespace -- an isolated storage space for an AI agent's own persistent memory records. The same real entity as cloudflare_memory, discovered via a distinct read path in Cloudflare's own spec.
cloudflare_nsc_cni: A Cloud Network Interconnect (CNI) -- a point-to-point link between Cloudflare's network and a customer's own network, configured with BGP (`bgp`, `bgp_mode` controlling the customer-facing routing mode) and the IP addressing (`cust_ip`, `p2p_ip`) for each end of the link.
cloudflare_observatory_page_test_respons: A Speed/Observatory page test -- triggers a synthetic performance test of `url` from a given `region`, the mechanism behind Cloudflare's own Observatory page-speed reports.
cloudflare_one_integration_detail_respon: A Zero Trust (Cloudflare One) SaaS integration -- connects a third-party application (`application`, e.g. Google Workspace, AWS) via `auth_method` and `credentials`, with `dlp_profiles` and `permissions` scoping what DLP/CASB visibility and control Cloudflare gets into that application.
cloudflare_organization: A Cloudflare Organization -- a real, distinct multi-account management concept (Tenant's own top-level grouping) above individual accounts, with an optional `parent` organization and its own `profile`/`meta` for organization-level settings.
cloudflare_origin_cloud_region: An origin cloud region mapping for zone caching -- associates an origin IP address with the specific cloud vendor region it's hosted in, letting Cloudflare route or cache traffic with awareness of the origin's own real cloud placement.
cloudflare_pagerule: A (legacy) Page Rule for a zone. Matches requests against `targets` (URL patterns) and either redirects them or overrides zone settings (but not both) via `actions`, evaluated in `priority` order. Superseded for new configuration by the Ruleset Engine's own dynamic redirects and settings overrides, but still live for zones using the legacy product.
cloudflare_participant: A participant added to a RealtimeKit meeting -- represents one attendee, identified by a caller-supplied `custom_participant_id`, with `preset_name` applying a pre-configured role/permission set to that participant.
cloudflare_pipeline: A Cloudflare Pipeline -- a managed streaming ETL pipeline that processes ingested events through a `sql` transformation before writing them to a destination (e.g. an R2 bucket).
cloudflare_policy: A remediation policy in Data Security Posture Management (DSPM). Defines `actions` to take automatically when a specific `finding_type_id` is triggered, scoped to either all integrations or an explicit `integration_ids` list.
cloudflare_portal: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) portal in Access's AI Controls. Exposes one or more registered MCP `servers` at a given `hostname`, with `code_mode` controlling whether connecting clients may use Code Mode and `secure_web_gateway` optionally routing outbound MCP traffic through Zero Trust.
cloudflare_posture_api_export_job_respon: A content export job in Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) -- exports flagged content matching the given filters (DLP profile, integration, affliction date range, search term) for offline review.
cloudflare_posture_api_finding_instance_: An archive action on one or more DSPM finding instances -- marks the listed `check_instances` as archived, removing them from active review without deleting the underlying finding.
cloudflare_posture_api_finding_response: An ignore action on one or more DSPM findings -- marks the listed `checks` as ignored, suppressing them from active review.
cloudflare_posture_api_webhook_response: A webhook configuration for Data Security Posture Management (DSPM) -- sends DSPM findings/events to `destination_url`, with `authentication_type`/`signing_secret` configuring how the receiving endpoint verifies the request and `headers` adding custom request headers.
cloudflare_preset: A participant preset for RealtimeKit -- a named, reusable role/permission/UI configuration (`config`, `permissions`, `ui`) meetings assign to participants by `preset_name` instead of configuring each participant individually.
cloudflare_priority: Represents a query for prioritized Cloudforce One requests -- a paginated listing of requests, filtered/sorted by priority rather than a standalone priority entity in its own right.
cloudflare_project: A Cloudflare Pages project. Defines the connected source control repository (`source`), `build_config` for how to build it, `production_branch`, and per-environment `deployment_configs`.
cloudflare_query: A saved query in Cloudforce One's threat intelligence platform. Stores `query_json` (the query parameters) under a unique `name`, with optional alerting (`alert_enabled`, `alert_rollup_enabled`) and WAF-rule-list integration (`rule_enabled`, `rule_list_id`) for automatically blocking on matches.
cloudflare_queue: A Cloudflare Queue -- a managed message queue Workers can produce to and consume from, identified by `queue_name`.
cloudflare_realtimekit_webhook_success_r: A webhook for RealtimeKit -- sends selected meeting `events` to `url` when `enabled`, the mechanism by which an application is notified of real-time meeting activity outside the SDK's own client-side callbacks.
cloudflare_recording: A recording of a RealtimeKit meeting (`meeting_id`). Configures audio/interactive recording settings, an optional custom `url` to record an arbitrary screen instead of the meeting itself, storage destination (`storage_config`, `realtimekit_bucket_config`), and whether multiple concurrent recordings are allowed for the same meeting.
cloudflare_regional_hostname: A regional hostname -- restricts where a given zone subdomain's traffic is processed (`region_key`) and how it's routed (`routing`), part of Cloudflare's Data Localization Suite.
cloudflare_registrar_api_registration_re: A domain registration through Cloudflare Registrar. Registers `domain_name` for a term of `years`, with `contacts`/`contact_extensions` providing the required registrant data, `privacy_mode` controlling WHOIS redaction, and `auto_renew` opting into automatic renewal billing.
cloudflare_registrar_api_sandbox_registr: A domain registration through Cloudflare Registrar's sandbox environment -- the same real shape as cloudflare_registrar_api_registration_response_single, used for testing registration flows without a live registry transaction.
cloudflare_relay: A relay for Media over QUIC (MoQ) -- a named Cloudflare-managed relay endpoint used to publish and subscribe to MoQ media streams.
cloudflare_repo: A repository in Cloudflare's Artifacts (container registry) service. The same real entity and endpoint as cloudflare_commit (see that entry's own intro for the real noun-derivation mismatch there) -- `default_branch`/`read_only` describe the repository itself, not an individual commit.
cloudflare_request: Represents a query for Cloudforce One requests -- a paginated, filterable/sortable listing of requests by status and creation/completion time range, rather than a standalone request entity in its own right.
cloudflare_resource_group: A resource group for account-level IAM. Defines a `scope` (a set of scope objects narrowing which real account resources it covers), referenced by IAM role bindings to grant permissions over that specific resource subset instead of the whole account.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_exclud: An excluded recipient on a Resource Sharing share -- when a share targets a whole organization, explicitly excludes one account (`account_id`) from receiving it.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_recipi: A recipient on a Resource Sharing share -- grants a specific account (`recipient_account_id`) access to the resources included in the parent share.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_resour: A resource included in a Resource Sharing share -- references one account-owned resource (`resource_id`, `resource_type`) made available to the share's own recipients.
cloudflare_resource_sharing_share_respon: A Resource Sharing share -- the top-level container that groups a set of `resources` and grants access to a set of `recipients` (individual accounts or, via an exclusion list, a whole organization).
cloudflare_route: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_rule: A DEX (Digital Experience Monitoring) rule -- matches traffic via a wirefilter `match` expression, used to scope which traffic DEX tests and monitoring apply to.
cloudflare_rum_site_response_single: A Real User Monitoring (RUM) site. Configures the hostname RUM's own JavaScript beacon reports under, with `auto_install` controlling whether Cloudflare automatically injects the beacon for orange-clouded (proxied) sites.
cloudflare_scan: A URL scan job in Cloudflare's URL Scanner -- submits `url` for automated analysis (with optional custom headers and geo-egress `country`), returning screenshots and scan results once complete. `visibility` controls whether the scan appears in public listings.
cloudflare_secondary_dns_single_response: A Secondary DNS TSIG key -- authenticates zone transfers between Cloudflare and a primary/secondary nameserver pair using the given `algo` and shared `secret`.
A Secondary DNS peer -- a named remote nameserver Cloudflare performs zone transfers with, referenced by Secondary DNS zone configuration.
A Secondary DNS ACL -- an allowed IP range for primary/secondary nameservers performing zone transfers with Cloudflare's Secondary DNS, applied account-wide.
cloudflare_secrets_store_secret_response: The result of duplicating a Secrets Store secret -- creates a new secret (`name`, `comment`, `scopes`) as a copy of an existing one, scoped to the services listed in `scopes`.
cloudflare_secrets_store_store_response: A Secrets Store -- a named, account-level container for secrets, scoped by which Cloudflare services can read from it.
cloudflare_sensitivity_group: A DLP sensitivity group -- a named collection of sensitivity levels (`levels`), either explicit or seeded from a built-in `template_id`, that DLP profiles reference to weight how matches within the group should be treated.
cloudflare_server: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server registered with Access's AI Controls. Configures how Access connects to the upstream MCP endpoint (`hostname`, `auth_type`, `auth_credentials`), optionally routing outbound traffic through Zero Trust Secure Web Gateway.
cloudflare_sink: A sink for a Cloudflare Pipeline -- the destination an ETL pipeline writes processed events to (currently R2, per `config`), with `format`/`schema` describing the shape of the written data.
cloudflare_smartshield_single_hc_respons: A Smart Shield health check -- the same real health-check concept as cloudflare_healthchecks_single_response, scoped to Cloudflare's Smart Shield product rather than the general zone health-checks endpoint.
cloudflare_stream: A stream for a Cloudflare Pipeline -- an HTTP ingestion endpoint (`http`) or Worker binding (`worker_binding`) events are pushed into before the pipeline's own SQL processing and sink delivery.
cloudflare_stream_language_response_sing: A caption/subtitle track for a Cloudflare Stream video, in a specific `language` -- uploaded as a WebVTT file.
cloudflare_stream_live_input_response_si: A live input for Cloudflare Stream -- an ingest endpoint for a live broadcast. Configures recording behavior (`recording`, `delete_recording_after_days`) and low-latency delivery (`prefer_low_latency`) for the resulting stream.
cloudflare_stream_video_response_single: A Cloudflare Stream video, created by copying from an external `url`/`input`. Configures access control (`require_signed_urls`, `allowed_origins`), an optional `scheduled_deletion` time, and thumbnail generation.
cloudflare_stream_watermark_response_sin: A watermark profile for Cloudflare Stream -- a reusable overlay image (`url`) with configurable position, scale, opacity, and padding, applied to videos that reference the profile.
cloudflare_subscription: An event subscription in Cloudflare's Event Notifications platform. Routes matching `events` from a `source` configuration to a `destination`, the mechanism behind Cloudflare's own webhook/queue-based event delivery for account activity.
cloudflare_suppression: An email suppression entry for Email Routing -- an `email` address (with an optional `expires_at`) Cloudflare stops delivering routed mail to, typically added after a hard bounce.
cloudflare_takedown_notice: A takedown notice in Cloudforce One's Brand Protection service -- tracks the lifecycle (`status`) of a takedown request against an infringing `domain`, linked to the `match_id`/`match_type` that triggered it and the letters (see cloudflare_letter) sent as part of the process.
cloudflare_target: An infrastructure target for Cloudflare's Infrastructure Access product -- a non-unique `hostname` and `ip` pair identifying a real machine or service that Zero Trust access policies can target for SSH/RDP-style access.
cloudflare_target_environment: A target environment for Vulnerability Scanner -- identifies a Cloudflare asset (currently zone-typed only, via `target`'s own discriminator) the scanner is authorized to scan.
cloudflare_teams_devices_components_sche: A device managed network for Zero Trust -- defines how the WARP client detects it's on a specific trusted network (`config`, `type`), used to apply network-aware device policies.
cloudflare_teams_devices_device_settings: A WARP client device settings policy -- account-wide (or matched-device) configuration for WARP client behavior: mode switching, auto-connect/reconnect timing, captive portal handling, DNS search suffixes, and tunnel route inclusion/exclusion.
cloudflare_teams_devices_schemas_single_: A device posture integration for Zero Trust -- connects a third-party posture-check API (`type`, `config`) that WARP client posture rules can reference, polled on the given `interval`.
cloudflare_teams_devices_single_response: A device posture rule for Zero Trust -- a named check (`type`, `match`, `input`) evaluated against a device on a polling `schedule`, whose pass/fail result feeds Access policies' own device-posture conditions.
cloudflare_template: A letter template in Cloudforce One's Brand Protection service -- reusable takedown-notice text (`body`, `category`, `source`) that takedown notice letters are generated from.
cloudflare_tls_certificates_and_hostname: A custom SSL/TLS certificate uploaded to a zone -- `certificate`/`private_key` (or a reference to an already-submitted CSR via `custom_csr_id`), with `geo_restrictions`/`policy` controlling where the private key may be held.
A Cloudflare Origin CA certificate -- issued by Cloudflare's own origin certificate authority for the `hostnames` listed, from a submitted `csr`, valid for `requested_validity` days.
The zone-level Authenticated Origin Pulls certificate -- the client certificate Cloudflare presents to the zone's own origin server to authenticate edge-to-origin requests.

A per-hostname Authenticated Origin Pulls certificate -- the same real mechanism as cloudflare_tls_certificates_and_hostnames_certificate_response_single_3, scoped to an individual custom hostname rather than the whole zone.

An account-level mTLS certificate -- a CA or leaf certificate (`ca` discriminates which) usable across the account wherever mutual TLS is needed, including as a custom certificate for Zero Trust's own block page.
A zone-level client (mTLS) certificate -- issued from a submitted `csr`, valid for `validity_days`, used to authenticate client devices connecting to the zone.

A zone-level Certificate Signing Request (CSR) generated by Cloudflare -- `common_name`/`sans`/organization fields describe the certificate to be signed; the resulting CSR can be submitted to an external CA or used with `custom_csr_id` on a custom certificate upload.
An account-level Certificate Signing Request (CSR), the same real concept as cloudflare_tls_certificates_and_hostnames_custom_csr_response_single scoped to the account rather than a single zone.

A custom hostname for SSL for SaaS -- a customer-owned hostname (`hostname`) CNAMEd to the zone, with `ssl` controlling its own certificate provisioning and `custom_origin_server`/`custom_origin_sni` optionally routing it to a different origin than the zone's own default.
A zone-level custom trust store entry -- a root CA certificate Cloudflare trusts when validating a client or origin connection, beyond the public CAs trusted by default.

A Keyless SSL certificate configuration -- lets Cloudflare terminate TLS for `host` while the private key stays on the customer's own Keyless SSL server (reached at `host`:`port`, optionally through a Cloudflare Tunnel), rather than uploading the key to Cloudflare.

A per-hostname TLS setting override -- sets a specific TLS setting (`setting_id`, e.g. allowed cipher suites) for a single `hostname` within the zone, distinct from the zone's own default TLS configuration.
cloudflare_token: An API token for AI Search -- credentials (`cf_api_id`/`cf_api_key`) an AI Search instance uses to call other Cloudflare APIs on the account's behalf.
cloudflare_tree: A repository in Cloudflare's Artifacts (container registry) service -- the same real entity and endpoint as cloudflare_commit and cloudflare_repo (see cloudflare_commit's own intro for the real noun-derivation mismatch shared by all three).
cloudflare_trigger: A Cron Trigger binding for a Worker script (`script_name`) -- schedules the named Worker to run on a cron schedule, configured via this endpoint's own request body rather than a separately-named field set (the response envelope carries no real trigger-specific fields beyond the generic success wrapper).
cloudflare_tunnel_cfd_tunnel_response_si: A Cloudflare Tunnel -- a persistent, outbound-only connection from an origin to Cloudflare's network. `config_src` distinguishes a locally-YAML-configured tunnel from one whose configuration is managed remotely via the API/dashboard.
cloudflare_tunnel_hostname_route_respons: A hostname route for Cloudflare Tunnel (Zero Trust networking) -- directs traffic for a specific `hostname` to the tunnel identified by `tunnel_id`.
cloudflare_tunnel_route_response_single: A network route for Cloudflare Tunnel -- directs traffic for a private IP `network` (CIDR) to the tunnel identified by `tunnel_id`, optionally scoped to a specific `virtual_network_id`.
cloudflare_tunnel_subnet_response_single: A WARP subnet for Zero Trust networking -- a private IP range (`network`) WARP-connected devices can reach, with `is_default_network` marking the account's own single default subnet.
cloudflare_tunnel_vnet_response_single: A virtual network for Cloudflare Tunnel -- an isolated routing namespace tunnel routes can be scoped to, letting the same private IP ranges be reused across separate virtual networks without conflict. `is_default`/`is_default_network` mark the account's own default.
cloudflare_tunnel_warp_connector_respons: A WARP Connector -- a Cloudflare Tunnel variant purpose-built to connect a private network to Cloudflare's Zero Trust WARP overlay, with `ha` opting into a highly-available multi-connector setup.
cloudflare_url: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_url_ignore_pattern: A URL ignore pattern for Email Security -- a regular expression (`pattern`) identifying URLs that should be exempt from Email Security's own link-rewriting/scanning behavior.
cloudflare_user_group: A User group for account-level IAM -- a named collection of IAM `policies` assigned as a unit to users, instead of attaching policies to each user individually.
cloudflare_user_schema: A user-uploaded API schema for API Shield's schema validation feature -- the same real concept as cloudflare_api_shield_public_schema_success_result, discovered via a distinct read path that emphasizes the schema's own `file`-upload creation flow.
cloudflare_version: An AI Gateway, despite its own generated name -- the same real entity as cloudflare_gateway and its sibling generated names (see cloudflare_dataset's own intro for the full list). A real noun-derivation mismatch, not a docs gap.
cloudflare_waf_product_api_bundle_respon: A custom leaked-credential-check detection for the WAF -- a zone-level rule matching `username`/`password` fields in request bodies against ruleset expressions, extending Cloudflare's own built-in leaked-credential detections with account-specific ones.
cloudflare_waitingroom_event_response: A scheduled event for a Waiting Room -- temporarily overrides the parent waiting room's own settings (queueing method, session duration, custom page, new-user admission rate) for the duration between `event_start_time` and `event_end_time`, reverting to the room's own defaults for any field left null.
cloudflare_waitingroom_single_response: A Waiting Room for a zone -- queues visitors to `host` (and optionally specific paths, via `additional_routes` on Advanced plans) when origin capacity is constrained, controlling queue behavior, cookie handling, and the rendered waiting page.
cloudflare_web3_content_list_entry_singl: A content list entry for a Web3/IPFS gateway hostname -- blocks a specific IPFS `content` (CID or content path) of the given `type` from being served through the gateway.
cloudflare_web3_single_response: A Web3 hostname -- a zone hostname that gateways requests to a decentralized `target` (e.g. IPFS, via `dnslink`), letting a normal DNS-resolvable hostname serve content from a Web3 network.
cloudflare_widget: A Turnstile widget -- Cloudflare's CAPTCHA alternative. Configures challenge behavior (`mode`, `bot_fight_mode`), which `domains` it's valid on, branding (`offlabel`), and the availability `region`, identified by its own `sitekey`.
cloudflare_worker: A Workers Build configuration -- connects a Worker to a `git_repository` for CI-driven deployment, with `production_settings` controlling the build/deploy behavior for production pushes.
cloudflare_workers_namespace_single_resp: A Workers for Platforms dispatch namespace -- an isolated deployment target multiple customer Workers ('user Workers') can be deployed into, then dynamically dispatched to from a single entrypoint Worker.
cloudflare_workers_versions_single_respo: A version of a Worker script (`script_name`) -- an uploaded, immutable snapshot of the script's own `files`/`metadata` at a point in time, referenced by `version_id`. A script's own gradual/canary deployments select traffic percentages across versions rather than replacing the live script outright.
cloudflare_workflow: A Cloudflare Workflow -- a durable-execution definition (`class_name` naming the Worker class implementing it, `script_name` the owning Worker) with configurable `concurrency`, `limits`, `schedules`, and `default_retention` for its own run instances.
cloudflare_zero_trust_gateway_list_singl: A Gateway list -- a named, reusable collection of `items` (e.g. domains, IPs) Zero Trust Gateway policies reference by list instead of enumerating values inline.
cloudflare_zero_trust_gateway_single_res: A Gateway certificate -- the TLS certificate Zero Trust Gateway uses for TLS decryption/inspection, with `validity_period_days` controlling the certificate's own lifetime.

A Gateway location -- a named network location (identified by its own `networks`/CIDR ranges) DNS/HTTP/network policies can be scoped to, with `client_default` marking the account's own default location and `dns_destination_ips_id` binding it to a specific pair of resolver IPs.

A Gateway rule -- the core policy unit of Zero Trust Secure Web Gateway. Matches traffic via `filters`/`identity`/`device_posture` wirefilter expressions and applies `action` when matched, evaluated across rules in ascending `precedence` order.

A Gateway proxy endpoint -- a dedicated IP/port Zero Trust Gateway exposes for a specific proxy `kind`, used when traffic needs to reach Gateway through a fixed, dedicated address rather than the shared WARP/PAC-file path.

A Gateway PAC file -- a hosted Proxy Auto-Configuration file (`contents`) devices can be pointed at to route traffic through Zero Trust Gateway without the WARP client, addressable at a URL-friendly `slug`.
cloudflare_zone: A Cloudflare zone -- the core unit of the platform, representing a domain (`name`) onboarded to Cloudflare. `type` distinguishes a full zone (DNS hosted with Cloudflare) from a partial zone (partner-hosted DNS, Cloudflare added via CNAME).
data_cloudflare_aaa_alerts_response_coll: The list of available alert types for Cloudflare's Notifications service -- the catalog of `alert_type` values a Notification policy's own `alert_type` field can be set to.
data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_response_: An account's own audit log entries, filterable by action type, actor, and time range.
data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_v2: The full audit history for a single audit log entry (`id`) -- Audit Logs v2's own resource-history view, paginated via `cursor`.
data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_v2_org: The full audit history for a single audit log entry (`id`), scoped to an organization rather than an account -- the same real view as data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_v2.
data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_v2_org_re: An organization's own Audit Logs v2 entries, filterable by actor, action type/result, and more.
data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_v2_produc: The list of real Cloudflare product categories Audit Logs v2 entries can be filtered by.
data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_v2_respon: An account's own Audit Logs v2 entries, filterable by actor, action type/result, account name, and more -- the v2 successor to data_cloudflare_aaa_audit_logs_response_collection.
data_cloudflare_aaa_components_schemas_r: An account's configured PagerDuty destinations for Cloudflare's Notifications service.
data_cloudflare_aaa_schemas_response_col: The notification destinations (e.g. webhooks, PagerDuty) eligible to be used by Notification policies on this account.
data_cloudflare_aaa_silences_components_: An account's own active notification silences -- temporary suppressions of specific Notification policies.
data_cloudflare_aaa_unsubscribe_email_si: Processes an email-based unsubscribe request (`token`) from a specific Notification policy for the given `email` address.
data_cloudflare_aaa_webhooks_components_: An account's configured webhook destinations for Cloudflare's Notifications service.
data_cloudflare_abuse_report: An account's own submitted abuse reports, filterable by domain, mitigation status, and creation time range.
data_cloudflare_abuse_reports_email_list: The list of notification emails sent for a specific submitted abuse report (`report_id`).
data_cloudflare_abuse_reports_submitted_: The detail of a single submitted abuse report (`report_id`).
An account's own submitted abuse reports, filterable by domain and creation time range -- the same real listing as data_cloudflare_abuse_report, from the /submitted path.
data_cloudflare_access_active_session_re: A single active Access session (`nonce`) for a given Access user.
data_cloudflare_access_active_sessions_r: The active Access sessions for a given Access user.

data_cloudflare_access_failed_login_resp: The failed Access login attempts for a given Access user.
data_cloudflare_access_idp_federation_gr: An account's own Access identity provider federation grants.
data_cloudflare_access_last_seen_identit: The most recent Access identity (authentication details) seen for a given Access user.
